profile.reading:
At 2703 Ena Drive in Lansing, Michigan sits the larger of Liquid Web's two home-market data centers, and the one a facility-directory listing identifies as the company's headquarters building: roughly 90,000 square feet with about 50,000 square feet of technical white space, matching what Liquid Web's own site describes as its "Data Center B," sized for around 25,000 servers. Liquid Web is a privately held web hosting, managed hosting, and cloud infrastructure company founded in Lansing in 1997, and this campus -- alongside the smaller Data Center A a short distance away on South Creyts Road -- anchors the company's US-Central operating region.

Per Liquid Web's own published specifications for its Lansing facilities generally, backup power runs on multiple N+1 Generac diesel generators paired with multiple N+1 Powerware 9395 series UPS systems (550 kVA units), while cooling is handled by an array of Liebert precision-cooling units (20 to 45 tons each) run as standalone systems so a single unit's failure cannot take down the broader floor. The company reports 24/7/365 on-site staffing, CCTV coverage, and electronic access control, SSAE-18 audit compliance, and HIPAA/Safe Harbor eligibility for regulated workloads, along with a redundant fiber network expandable to 1,840 gigabits per second. Liquid Web markets more than 26 years of continuous uptime from its Lansing operations as of its latest published materials.

As with its sibling facility, Liquid Web does not publish a specific street address for this building on its own website; the 2703 Ena Drive address applied here comes from a facility-directory listing that independently matches this row's stored map coordinates via reverse geocoding, and whose stated size (90,000 square feet) and headquarters designation align with Liquid Web's own published Data Center B figures. Being the headquarters-designated building of the pair, this site plausibly houses more of Liquid Web's corporate and network-operations functions alongside colocation and hosting infrastructure, though the company does not publish that breakdown publicly. No permit or zoning record specific to this address was located to further confirm construction history, and no expansion announcements specific to this building (as opposed to the Lansing campus generally) were found in public reporting.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Liquid Web is a privately held web hosting and cloud services company headquartered in Lansing, Michigan, founded in 1997. This operators own site describes two Lansing area data centers, Data Center A at 32,000 square feet with capacity for 8,000 servers, and Data Center B at 90,000 square feet with capacity for 25,000 servers, but does not publish street addresses for either. This session found a facility specific aggregator listing naming three Lansing facilities with street addresses, DC1 at 4210 South Creyts Road, DC2 at 4428 South Creyts Road, and DC3 at 2703 Ena Drive, the latter identified as headquarters and described as a 90,000 square foot facility with 50,000 square feet of whitespace. The aggregators separately listed DC1 address does not match either of this registrys two Liquid Web rows and is not applied to any row.

reading.body:
Liquid Web operates a 90,000 square foot facility in Lansing, Michigan with stated capacity for 25,000 servers. The campus has a 13,500 kVA utility power feed across two buildings, though the operator does not publish IT load in megawatts. Assuming 5 kW per server, a conservative estimate for general hosting workloads, this would imply roughly 125 MW of IT demand if fully populated, but the actual power allocation between the two buildings and the proportion dedicated to compute versus supporting infrastructure is not published.

Michigan has six mapped data center facilities and no other published power capacity figures in this site's records, making Liquid Web's Lansing campus the only facility in the state with a disclosed power specification. The facility is located at the operator's headquarters and has been expanded to its current configuration, though growth trajectory and planned capacity additions are not published.

The campus is configured for general hosting and cloud services rather than GPU-intensive AI training based on the server count specification. No certifications for specific workload types are published on the operator's spec page. Whether this facility will matter to AI scaling depends on whether the operator adds published power figures and on whether compute density per rack increases toward levels required for large model training.
